name: org.machanism.machai:ghostwriter
description: Ghostwriter is a Java command-line documentation engine and project-wide AI-assisted file processing component from Machai. It scans source code, tests, documentation, Maven site content, configuration, diagrams, and other project artifacts; detects embedded @guidance instructions; and dispatches guided prompts to a configured GenAI provider. It supports two primary modes: Guidance mode, which uses file-format-aware reviewers to extract @guidance directives from Java, Markdown, HTML, XML, PlantUML, Python, TypeScript, and @guidance.txt files; and Act mode, which runs reusable TOML-defined workflows with inheritance, default values, prompt placeholders, episode selection, interactive chat behavior, and project-scoped context. Ghostwriter exposes host-side function tools for file operations, patching, command execution with logging, REST and web access, Act orchestration, guidance processing, episode control, execution control, and project context variables. It is useful for automated documentation generation, code documentation updates, guided repository maintenance, CI/CD documentation workflows, AI-assisted project analysis, reusable prompt workflow execution, and Maven/Java project automation.

integrations: Git and SVN workflows through command tools

constructors.description: Creates a guidance processor that scans project files for @guidance tags and sends extracted instructions to the configured GenAI model. The root directory defines the project boundary, genai identifies the provider or model, and the configurator supplies runtime properties.

examples.description: Creates a GuidanceProcessor for the current project and runs a targeted scan over Markdown files. Use this scenario when a host application wants to process embedded @guidance comments programmatically instead of invoking the CLI.

constructors.description: Creates an Act processor for TOML-defined reusable workflows. Acts can be loaded from built-in resources, custom directories, remote locations, or direct TOML paths and can run as one-shot commands or interactive multi-episode workflows.

examples.description: Creates an ActProcessor, points it to a custom Acts directory, and selects the general-purpose task Act with a user prompt. Use this when embedding Ghostwriter workflows inside another Java automation tool.

constructors.description: Creates the base AI-backed file processor used by both guidance and Act workflows. It prepares prompt metadata, resolves include markers, substitutes public configuration placeholders, registers function tools, and dispatches prompts to the configured GenAI provider.

examples.description: Creates the generic processor and configures shared instructions plus a default prompt. Use this lower-level entry point when building a custom processor or integration that reuses Ghostwriter prompt preparation behavior.

features.name: scanDocuments
features.signature: public void scanDocuments(java.io.File projectDir, java.lang.String path) throws java.io.IOException
features.description: Scans a project directory using a raw path, a glob pattern, or a regular expression pattern. The processor resolves the path inside the project boundary and processes matching files or folders. GuidanceProcessor uses this to find guided files; ActProcessor can also apply acts to selected paths.

examples.description: Runs guidance processing only for Maven site Markdown pages. This is practical for documentation generation jobs where source code should not be changed.

features.name: setAct
features.signature: public void setAct(java.lang.String act) throws java.io.IOException
features.description: Parses and configures an Act command. It supports blank commands defaulting to help, shorthand task commands beginning with >, inline user prompts, episode selection with #, multiple episode identifiers separated by commas, stop markers with !, default property application, and TOML-based Act loading with inheritance.

examples.description: Configures an Act to run only episodes 1 and 2 of the unit-tests workflow and then stop. Use this for controlled multi-step workflows in CI or focused local automation.

features.name: process
features.signature: public java.lang.String process(org.machanism.machai.project.layout.ProjectLayout projectLayout, java.io.File file, java.lang.String prompt)
features.description: Processes a specific file or project context with a prompt using the configured AI provider. The processor adds system instructions, process metadata, project layout details, placeholders, prompt includes, and enabled tool configuration before invoking the provider.

examples.description: Shows direct file processing with a simple prompt. A real integration supplies a populated ProjectLayout so Ghostwriter can include project metadata in the AI request.

features.name: perform
features.signature: public java.lang.String perform(java.io.File projectDir, java.io.File file) throws java.io.IOException
features.description: Reviewer implementations inspect a file, detect @guidance instructions using the comment syntax of that file type, and return a normalized prompt fragment. Built-in reviewers support Java, Markdown, HTML, XML, PlantUML, Python, TypeScript, and folder-level @guidance.txt files.

examples.description: Extracts a guidance prompt from a Markdown file. Use this when testing custom guidance content before a full project scan.

features.name: executeCommand
features.signature: public java.lang.Object executeCommand(java.lang.String command, java.util.Map<java.lang.String,java.lang.String> properties, java.lang.String dir, int tailResultSize, java.lang.String charsetName, java.io.File projectDir, org.machanism.macha.core.commons.configurator.Configurator configurator) throws java.io.IOException
features.description: Executes an allowed operating-system command in a project-relative working directory, applies command security checks, captures bounded output, persists a command log, and returns a structured report with exit code and log metadata. It is used by function-tool workflows for builds, tests, diagnostics, and controlled automation.

examples.snippet:
org.machanism.machai.gw.tools.CommandFunctionTools tools = new org.machanism.machai.gw.tools.CommandFunctionTools();
java.lang.Object report = tools.executeCommand("mvn -q test", null, ".", 4096, "UTF-8", new java.io.File("."), null);
examples.description: Runs Maven tests from the current project and captures the result. This is useful inside an Act that must validate generated documentation or code changes before finishing.

customizations.name: Custom Act TOML files
customizations.description: Users can define reusable workflows in TOML files, place them in a configured acts directory, inherit from built-in Acts with basedOn, add default values in a [default] section, and use ${public.prompt} or other placeholders for runtime substitution.

examples.snippet:
description = '''Reviews project documentation.'''
instructions = '''You are a helpful technical writer.'''
inputs = '''Review the documentation and suggest improvements.\n\n${public.prompt}'''
[default]
gw.path = "glob:src/site/**"
public.prompt = "Focus on first-time users."
examples.description: A practical custom Act that can be saved as review-docs.toml and invoked with --act review-docs. It scopes processing to site documentation and provides a default user prompt.

customizations.name: Reviewer service provider implementations
customizations.description: The Reviewer SPI can be implemented to support additional file formats or custom guidance extraction rules. A reviewer declares supported extensions and returns a prompt fragment when guidance is present.

examples.description: A minimal custom reviewer skeleton. Register it through Java service loading so GuidanceProcessor can discover the new file type.

studs.name: org.machanism.machai.gw.reviewer.Reviewer
studs.description: Service-provider interface for scanning project files and extracting @guidance instructions. Implementations understand file-specific comment conventions and return normalized prompt fragments for Ghostwriter processing.

examples.snippet:
org.machanism.machai.gw.reviewer.Reviewer reviewer = new org.machanism.machai.gw.reviewer.JavaReviewer();
java.lang.String[] extensions = reviewer.getSupportedFileExtensions();
examples.description: Uses the reviewer interface through the JavaReviewer implementation to inspect which extensions are supported.

studs.name: org.machanism.machai.gw.processor.AbstractFileProcessor
studs.description: Base class for processors that traverse project directories, filter files by include and exclude patterns, support module scanning, and delegate per-file processing to subclasses.

examples.snippet:
org.machanism.machai.gw.processor.AIFileProcessor processor = new org.machanism.machai.gw.processor.AIFileProcessor(new java.io.File("."), null, "OpenAI:gpt-4.1");
processor.setExcludes(new java.lang.String[] { "target", ".git" });
examples.description: Configures inherited file traversal behavior by excluding build and version-control directories.

examples.title: Install Ghostwriter as a Maven dependency
examples.scenario: Use Ghostwriter classes from a Java automation application.
steps: Add org.machanism.machai:ghostwriter:1.3.1 to the Maven project dependencies.
Provide a supported GenAI provider configuration through the Machai configurator or runtime properties.
Create a GuidanceProcessor or ActProcessor and run it against project files.
examples.description: This dependency configuration installs Ghostwriter from Maven Central for programmatic use in Java applications.

examples.title: Run the Ghostwriter CLI pack
examples.scenario: Process project Markdown files from the command line using embedded @guidance tags.
steps: Download and unzip the Ghostwriter CLI delivery pack from https://sourceforge.net/projects/machanism/files/machai/ghostwriter/gw.zip/download.
Configure provider credentials and model settings in the environment or Ghostwriter properties file.
Open a terminal in the project root directory.
Run the CLI with a glob pattern that targets the desired files.
Review generated changes and command logs before committing.
examples.snippet: java -jar gw.jar "glob:src/site/markdown/**/*.md" --model "OpenAI:gpt-4.1" --instructions "Keep language clear for first-time users."
examples.description: This is a practical how-to-use scenario for ready-to-run CLI usage. It installs the component by downloading the delivery pack, configures a model, and invokes a targeted documentation-processing run.

examples.title: Run a reusable Act workflow
examples.scenario: Use Act mode to run a predefined documentation or testing workflow.
steps: Create or select an Act TOML file such as review-docs.toml or use a built-in Act such as task, code-doc, unit-tests, or help.
Optionally configure a custom acts directory with --acts.
Invoke --act with the Act name and optional user prompt.
For interactive Acts, enter . to finish or > to continue without adding a new prompt.
examples.snippet: java -jar gw.jar --acts acts --act review-docs "Check whether examples explain installation, configuration, and execution."
examples.description: Demonstrates how to configure and run a reusable Act workflow in a real project. This is appropriate for repeated documentation reviews, code documentation passes, or test-generation tasks.
